config.androidShared: google-services.json holds every Android app in the project, so one file serves all of them.
config.android1: Move <file>google-services.json</file> into your app module's directory (usually app/).
config.android2: Apply the Google services Gradle plugin, which reads <file>google-services.json</file> at build time.
config.ios1: Drag <file>GoogleService-Info.plist</file> into the root of your Xcode project and add it to every target.
config.web2: Add the configuration below to your app and initialize it.

app.title: App
app.deleteBody: Its config files stop working. You can restore the app within {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}; after that it's removed permanently.
app.deletedBody: Restore it before {date}; after that it's removed permanently.
app.configHint: Download it again whenever you need it; it is generated fresh each time.

sha.title: SHA certificate fingerprints
sha.description: Fingerprints of the certificates that sign this Android app.
sha.hint: A SHA-1 or SHA-256 fingerprint, with or without colons.

sha.howTo: How do I find my fingerprint?
sha.removeBody: Builds signed with this certificate will no longer match the app.

keys.title: API keys
keys.subtitle: Keys identify this project to the client SDKs.
keys.notSecretTitle: An API key is not a secret
keys.notSecretBody: API keys ship inside your apps and anyone can read them. They identify the project; they don't grant administrative access. Use restrictions to limit where a key is accepted.
keys.emptyBody: A key is created automatically with the first app of each platform.
keys.name: Name
keys.nameHint: Optional. Only shown in the console.
keys.rotateBody: A new key takes over this key's platform: config files you download from now on carry the new key.
keys.rotateOldKey: The old key keeps working until you disable it, so apps already released keep running while you update them.
keys.rotated: New key created. Disable the old one once your apps use the new key.
keys.disableBody: Every request that presents this key will be refused, including from apps already released. You can enable it again.

kindHint.none: The key is accepted from anywhere.
kindHint.browser: Accept the key only from these websites.
kindHint.android: Accept the key only from these Android apps.
kindHint.ios: Accept the key only from these iOS apps.

summary.ios: {count, plural, one {# iOS app} other {# iOS apps}}

keys.badBundleId: Each bundle ID must look like com.example.app.

problem.empty: Add at least one app, or choose no restriction.

problem.sha1: Each app needs a SHA-1 fingerprint (40 hex digits).

serviceAccounts.idTaken: A service account with this ID already exists in the project.
serviceAccounts.emptyBody: Create one for each server or tool that needs administrative access.
serviceAccounts.noKeys: No keys. Generate one to use this account from a server.
serviceAccounts.generateBody: A JSON key file is downloaded to this device.
serviceAccounts.onceBody: Aruma doesn't keep the private key, so the file can't be downloaded again. Store it safely; anyone who has it can act as this service account.
serviceAccounts.keyLimit: This account has the maximum of {max} keys. Delete one to generate another.
serviceAccounts.deleteKeyBody: Servers using this key file lose access at once.
serviceAccounts.deleteBody: {email} and all its keys and tokens stop working at once. This can't be undone.
